item.title: Want to Stand Out at Work? Avoid These Top 10 Email Clichés
item.description: If you “reach out” and “circle back” often in your work emails, you’re not alone. These phrases are among the most overused email clichés around the world, a new study finds. Email has been around for more than 50 years, and it’s still the backbone of workplace communication. item.title: Study Finds Americans Overestimate Harmful Behavior on Social Media
item.description: A study published in PNAS Nexus reports that Americans consistently overestimate how many social media users post harmful content online. Across three national studies involving 1,090 U.S. adults, participants believed large shares of users on platforms such as Reddit and Facebook engaged in toxic language or shared false news. item.title: Global Report Flags Rising Use of Digital Controls to Suppress Dissent
item.description: A 2025 report by the University of Rhode Island’s Center for Nonviolence and Peace Studies documents a global rise in what researchers describe as digital repression by governments. Drawing on the CIRIGHTS Data Project and country human rights reports, the study finds that states increasingly rely on surveillance and legal pressure to discourage journalists and citizens from criticizing authorities. item.title: JP Conte: Five Things You Need To Successfully Build Strategic Partnerships [Promoted]
item.description: Private equity professionals often speak about returns, multiples, and exit timelines. JP Conte, managing partner of a San Francisco-based private equity firm and founder of family office Lupine Crest Capital, tends to speak about something else: relationships. Over a career spanning three decades — one that has seen his firm grow from approximately $100 million to $49 billion in assets under management — Conte has developed a distinctive philosophy about what makes partnerships succeed or fail.

item.description: Researchers have developed the first scientifically validated ‘personality test’ framework for popular AI chatbots, and have shown that chatbots not only mimic human personality traits, but their ‘personality’ can be reliably tested and precisely shaped – raising implications for AI safety and ethics. item.title: Task scams are up 485% in 2025 and job seekers are losing millions
item.description: The U.S. unemployment rate has been steadily rising since May, reaching 4.6% in November - the highest level seen since September 2021. Scammers are taking full advantage of the situation with “task scams”, also known as “gamified job scams”.
